basic_info.description_header: 👋  Hi I'm Jon, a software developer and .NET enthusiast.  👋
description: I am a Software Developer with experience in software testing, systems administration, project planning, and team leadership.
I began my career in technology as a Helpdesk Associate, moving up to a Computer Lab Technician, and later as a Windows Systems Administrator.
While earning my AAS in Network Technologies I created an asset-tracking database tool for the campus IT, which helped them track asset lifecycle and budget forecasting.

As a Systems Administrator at Citrix Systems, I managed the computer lab hardware, data storage, and network systems for a small developer lab. At the time the computer lab needed better management of resource sharing for developers to effectively perform their duties. So in conjunction with one of the software developers I helped design and deploy a hardware management tool that improved lab equipment utilization, and provided insight into asset sharing and lifecycle.

Facilities and IT were both off-site so I was largely responsible for managing electrical, cooling, and asset maintenance and upgrades, acquiring bids for work and managing lifecycle and budget forecasting. Other accomplishments include deploying, managing, and maintaining a globally accessible SharePoint site for the Engineering group.

As I gained more interest in engineering, I earned a certification in Software Test Engineering from Bellevue College where I picked up some experience with Python, C#, Git, SQL, and agile software development processes. Soon after, I moved into a software testing role at Citrix, designing test plans, executing and reporting on test/bug status, and contributing concrete, succinct bug report on locally developed software. During this time I also developed automated build-and-deploy scripts using PowerShell, and created a custom double-click-to-run UI testing system using Selenium Driver and Python.

My thirst for learning continued and I earned a certificate in Advanced Software Development in Java from Code Fellows in Seattle, WA. Many long days and nights were spent learning HTML 5, CSS, and JavaScript, the MERN stack, as well as Java and Spring Boot framework. In addition, I picked up experience in agile software development, managing git repositories, and was introduced to team and software project management. Many days of collaborative software development provided a solid foundation with techniques like pair-programming and use of tools like Trello Miro for project management and design.

I enjoy developing software solutions for web and desktop, working with engaging people, and finding solutions that make sense for the context of the end user. I look forward to working on a diverse software development team creating and refining technical solutions that delight customers.

When I'm not working on software projects, I can be found out riding my bike, or volunteering with groups like the National MS Society, Destination Trail, Snohomish County DEM, and Redmond Cycling Club.

projects.title: Winlink Forms Training
projects.description:
A colleague asked me to teach his team of ham radio volunteers how to create custom Winlink Templates and Forms. The goal was to prepare them to create custom forms for capturing and sharing situational awareness information with local ham radio stations, and to the Seattle Office of Emergency Management.
I developed the curriculum and training modules, and presented a slide deck and guided hands-on coding with a group of 1/2 dozen attendees.

projects.title: BF-BMX
projects.description: Many of my volunteer adventures include tracking cyclists or runners on a course. For one event, Bigfoot 200, hams use "email over ham radio" to send in runner reports. I developed a multi-project solution using DotNET 8 and WPF that watches for these reports, parses and logs the location data, and then posts the data to an ASP.NET Minimal API Server with an Entity Framework Core DB. The ham responsible for maintaining runner locations, can run reports against the logged data and answer questions like which runners has passed through a specific Aid Station. While specific to Bigfoot 200, the project is designed to be adaptable to other events. This project was designed to work in conjunction with the Bigfoot Bib Report Form project, and had its first trial-run in August 2024.

projects.title: Create Markdown TOC
projects.description: Some markdown files can get rather large with lots of headings, making it difficult to find information within. Using a table of contents speeds locating sections of interest, making it easier to find what you are looking for. With this extension, you can generate a table of contents in your markdown file without having to manually find and type out each heading.

projects.title: LingoBingo JS
projects.description: Working in our spare time, Ryan Shafer and I re-wrote the LingoBingo project using React. We are are finishing up the first part of a v.1 release that implements MERN-stack design pattern, and will follow that with an add-on UI for Presenters to add their own words and generate a web-link to their custom-defined LingoBingo boards.

projects.title: Bigfoot Bib Report Form
projects.description: Destination Trail holds an annual ultramarathon event in the Gifford-Pinchot Nat'l Forest in SW Washington State called Bigfoot 200. Hams from all around Washington and Oregon volunteer to provide communications for this event including, information on runner locations, as well as logistical and emergency communications with Net Control near the event base. The Winlink Development Team (www.winlink.org) developed a form to capture participant data at checkpoints or Aid Stations for events like this. I cleaned-up and customized the form using HTML 5, CSS 3, and JavaScript to meet the needs of Aid Station HAMs while tracking runners for this event. Design improvements include: Use of accessible colors and fonts, selected control highlighting, keyboard navigation, and a responsive UI for desktop, mobile, and tablet devices. Features include: Automated subject line generation, comma-separated data display, and data backup and restore, allowing standalone form usage so a HAM can fill out the form, save the data, and then sneaker net it to a Winlink station for transmission. Every year the form is updated with new features and improvements using input from the HAMs who use it.

projects.title: EZ-PC Shopper
projects.description: Final project for CodeFellows Code 201 class, designed to help web site users build and buy a computer system regardless of their knowledge of computers. This project challenged me to refine my bug finding and squashing skills, acquire a deeper understanding of CSS 3.0, and experience project management by guiding meetings, assisting with UI and functional design, and exercise pair-programming with my team mates.

projects.title: Salmon Cookies
projects.description: Code Fellows Code 201 Lab Project Cookie Stand provided an opportunity to put together JavaScript, HTML 5, CSS 3.0 to meet the goal of presenting a new website for a ficticious, growing business. The website uses HTML 5, CSS 3, and JavaScript. DOM manipulation is used to edit the UI to respond to user inputs and changes in stored data. HTML Forms and other structural tags, along with CSS features, were chosen carefully to make the site responsive, supporting phone-sized viewports. Managing images, content, and style were the focus features of this project, and I am proud of my very first JavaScript-enabled website project.

projects.title: LingoBingo
projects.description: One of the first web apps I worked on using C# DotNET Blazor Web Assembly. The original idea came from a webinar on audience engagement by Cindy Huggett, where she suggested presenters play Buzzword Bingo so audience members could yell BINGO when they match 5 presenter-planned buzzwords in a row. The project has been through many version, from Console application to what it is now - a live, playable Azure WebApp. I learned a lot about C#, Dot NET, and web development, which made it clear to me I wanted to learn more about building capable, fun websites!

projects.title: Coordinate Converter
projects.description: As an amateur radio operator I need to be aware of several different coordinate systems to identify where I am, and where other operators might be. As a software developer I want to develop an application that will help me convert from 4 common coordinate system notations. Many hams before me have explored solving coordinate conversion in software however I enjoyed the challenge and the achievement.
